canvas-01-1.description: The lower left of Sheet 1, below the key map and index, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north about 38 degrees clockwise of the page. It covers the east side of High Bridge south of the Taylor-Wharton steel works: Washington Avenue (Mill) along the top with Dewey Avenue joining it from the left, East Main Street running down the sheet, Maryland Avenue and Highland Avenue, Elm (High) Street between them, and Tisco Avenue curving away to the upper right with a row of company houses on its outer side. The southern end of the steel works (sheet 4) is sketched at the top, with tracks, a scrap breaking crane and yard buildings. A private reservoir lies between Maryland and Tisco Avenues. The blocks along East Main Street, Maryland Avenue and Washington Avenue are built up with frame dwellings, with a barber shop, meat market and auto supply store near the corner of Washington Avenue and East Main Street, a fire alarm at Elm Street and a store and auto shed on Highland Avenue. Large open blocks lie to the right, towards the heavy line dividing this part from the East Main Street and Highland Avenue part.
notes: Washington Avenue is also lettered Av. (Mill) here; Elm Street is also lettered (High).
Elm Street / Highland Avenue was hand-picked (a fire alarm symbol is printed on the junction).
The sheet's top half (key map, index, water and fire department notes) is outside this part.

Printed sheet 1, 100 ft to an inch. Top half is the key map (borough at about 1000 ft to an inch), index of specials, water and fire notes and the location map of New Jersey: left out of the masks. Bottom half has two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 Washington Avenue (Mill), East Main Street, Dewey, Maryland and Tisco Avenues, Elm (High) Street, Highland Avenue (north about 39 degrees); part 2 East Main Street and Highland Avenue south to Nassau Road (north about 75 degrees).

canvas-01-2.description: The lower right of Sheet 1, separated from the main part by a heavy diagonal line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north about 75 degrees clockwise of the page. It shows East Main Street and Highland Avenue running down the sheet side by side, joined by a short street marked not named, with Nassau Road leaving Highland Avenue at the bottom right. Frame dwellings stand along both sides of East Main Street, most with house numbers in the 300s, and a fire alarm box stands on East Main Street; the lots on Highland Avenue are laid out but only partly built. Large open blocks lie to the left of East Main Street and to the right of Highland Avenue. The part was placed from one hand-picked junction, Highland Avenue and Nassau Road, with the scale of the sheet and the direction of its north arrow.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked point (Highland Avenue / Nassau Road) with rotation from the north arrow. Low confidence away from that junction.
The short street between East Main Street and Highland Avenue is marked not named.

Printed sheet 1, 100 ft to an inch. Top half is the key map (borough at about 1000 ft to an inch), index of specials, water and fire notes and the location map of New Jersey: left out of the masks. Bottom half has two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 Washington Avenue (Mill), East Main Street, Dewey, Maryland and Tisco Avenues, Elm (High) Street, Highland Avenue (north about 39 degrees); part 2 East Main Street and Highland Avenue south to Nassau Road (north about 75 degrees).

sheet-2-1.description: The centre of High Bridge on Sheet 2, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the left of the page. The part runs from Church Street along the left edge, with the parallel Thomas, Taylor and Mill Streets crossing it, south through the business blocks on Main and Center Streets to the Central Railroad of New Jersey main line and the streets beyond it: Railroad Avenue, Bridge Street, West Street, Union Avenue and Hart Street, with the brook and the South Branch of the Raritan River at the bottom and right. The C.R.R. of N.J. Dover Branch runs down the left side of the part in a cutting beside Church Street, crossed by a wooden bridge at Thomas Street, and a railroad siding curves off it towards Mac Donald Street. The public school stands between Thomas and Taylor Streets, the M.E. church on Church Street, the American Hotel, a Roman Catholic church and the fire department on Main and Center Streets, the depot, baggage and freight houses and the Union Hotel along the tracks, Robert Apgar's coal yard by the Dover Branch, and the Diamond Flake Graphite Co. crushing and concentrating plant on the brook at the bottom. Prospect Street is marked not opened and a street east of Mac Donald Street is marked not named, not opened. Most lots between Thomas and Mill Streets are built with frame dwellings. The upper right of the sheet, cut off by heavy lines, holds two separately oriented parts (Beaver Street, and Arch Street with Washington Avenue), which are separate annotations.
notes: Railroad Avenue is now Central Avenue; West Street and the street marked (Main) below Hart Street are now part of West Main Street.
Union Avenue is also lettered (Main) on the sheet.
Van Sickle Street is spelled Van Syckle Street in OpenStreetMap.
Mill Street east of Mac Donald Street continues as Washington Avenue.
The C.R.R. of N.J. Dover Branch along Church Street is now the Columbia Trail.
The junctions of Hart Street with Central and Union Avenues and of Center and Van Sickle Streets lie 8 to 16 m from their modern positions and were rejected.

Printed sheet 2, 100 ft to an inch, north to the left (about -73 degrees). Three parts: part 1 the centre (Church, Thomas, Taylor, Mill, Main, Center, Mac Donald, Van Sickle, Railroad Avenue, Bridge, West, Union Avenue (Main), Hart Streets, C.R.R. of N.J. depot); part 2 a wedge with Beaver Street west of West (Main) Street and Clinton Road at the South Branch bridge (north about -80 degrees); part 3 Arch (School) Street and Washington Avenue (Mill) east of the river (north about -67 degrees).

sheet-2-2.description: A narrow wedge at the top of Sheet 2, outlined by heavy lines and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the left (about 80 degrees anticlockwise of the page). It shows Beaver Street running down from its junction with West Street, where the road from the steel bridge over the South Branch of the Raritan River (Clinton Road) also comes in. Frame dwellings stand on both sides of Beaver Street, with a garage at the corner of West Street; the lots east of Beaver Street are marked no exposure along the dividing line. The same junction is drawn at the lower right corner of the main part of the sheet, where Beaver Street leaves the bottom edge, so this wedge continues the main map to the west of West Main Street. The part has no other street junction; it was placed from that one junction, carried from the main part of the sheet, with the scale of the sheet and the direction of its own north arrow.
notes: Beaver Street is now Beavers Street; West Street is now West Main Street.
The road from the steel bridge (Clinton Road) is now Arch Street.
Placed from one point only (the West Street / Beaver Street junction carried from sheet 2 part 1); rotation from the north arrow. Low confidence away from the junction.

Printed sheet 2, 100 ft to an inch, north to the left (about -73 degrees). Three parts: part 1 the centre (Church, Thomas, Taylor, Mill, Main, Center, Mac Donald, Van Sickle, Railroad Avenue, Bridge, West, Union Avenue (Main), Hart Streets, C.R.R. of N.J. depot); part 2 a wedge with Beaver Street west of West (Main) Street and Clinton Road at the South Branch bridge (north about -80 degrees); part 3 Arch (School) Street and Washington Avenue (Mill) east of the river (north about -67 degrees).

sheet-2-3.description: The upper right corner of Sheet 2, outlined by heavy lines and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north about 67 degrees anticlockwise of the page. It shows Arch Street, also lettered School, running down from its junction with Mill Street (Washington Avenue) and turning at the lower end, with Washington Avenue continuing north at the top right. Frame dwellings line both sides of Arch Street and a group of dwellings stands at the lower right; a fire alarm box stands at the junction. Large blocks, marked 38 and 39, are mostly open. The lots towards the river are marked no exposure along the dividing line with the Beaver Street wedge. The part has one street junction and was placed from it, using the scale of the sheet and the direction of the junction's measured street lines.
notes: Arch Street is also lettered (School) on the sheet; the modern name is Arch Street.
Mill Street here is now Washington Avenue.
Placed from one detected junction (Arch Street / Washington Avenue) with a derived second point; low confidence away from the junction.

Printed sheet 2, 100 ft to an inch, north to the left (about -73 degrees). Three parts: part 1 the centre (Church, Thomas, Taylor, Mill, Main, Center, Mac Donald, Van Sickle, Railroad Avenue, Bridge, West, Union Avenue (Main), Hart Streets, C.R.R. of N.J. depot); part 2 a wedge with Beaver Street west of West (Main) Street and Clinton Road at the South Branch bridge (north about -80 degrees); part 3 Arch (School) Street and Washington Avenue (Mill) east of the river (north about -67 degrees).

sheet-3-1.description: The northern part of High Bridge on Sheet 3, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north about 16 degrees clockwise of the page. Mill Street climbs diagonally from Church Street at the lower left to the upper right, where it bends north and continues as Silverthorn to the top of the sheet; a street marked not named leaves it at the top. Along the bottom runs Church Street, with Main Street, Taylor, Thomas and Seal Streets running up to Mine Road, and Mountain Avenue east of Seal Street. These blocks are built up with frame dwellings, many with automobile sheds and coops; the Reformed Church and its parsonage stand at Church and Mill Streets. The C.R.R. of N.J. Dover Branch crosses the lower left corner and runs up the right edge of the sheet. The area between Mill Street and the Dover Branch is mostly open land with a few houses, stone dwellings and barns. A heavy line cuts off the upper left of the sheet, which holds a separately oriented part (Fairview Avenue and German Valley Road at the borough limits), a separate annotation.
notes: Mill Street on this sheet is now Fairview Avenue (County Route 513); Silverthorn at the top right lies on the line of modern Fairview Avenue and Silverthorne Road.
The street marked not named at the top right meets Silverthorn at the modern Fairview Avenue / Cregar Road junction.
Mine Road / Seal Street was rejected (7.7 m from the fit); the east end of Mine Road has been realigned.
The C.R.R. of N.J. Dover Branch is now the Columbia Trail.

Printed sheet 3, 100 ft to an inch, north about 16 degrees. Part 1 Mill Street (now Fairview Avenue), Mine Road, Church, Taylor, Thomas and Seal Streets, Mountain Avenue, Silverthorn to the borough line; part 2 an outlined wedge at the upper left with Fairview Avenue, Silverthorn, German Valley Road and the reservoir at the borough limits (north about 4 degrees).

sheet-3-2.description: An outlined wedge at the upper left of Sheet 3, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing almost straight up. It shows the northern edge of the borough: Fairview Avenue curving north from a junction with a street marked not named, Silverthorn running north-east, and German Valley Road leaving Silverthorn to the east. A dash-dot line marks the borough limits across the top. The borough reservoir, an oval basin with a supply house and an 8-inch water pipe, lies at the upper left. The land is mostly open, with scattered frame and stone dwellings, barns and a few outbuildings along Fairview Avenue and Silverthorn; letters along the roads mark house positions. The part was placed from one junction, the foot of Fairview Avenue where the street marked not named comes in (today Fairview Avenue and Cregar Road), with the scale of the sheet and the direction of the part's north arrow.
notes: The street marked not named at the foot of Fairview Avenue is now Cregar Road.
Silverthorn and German Valley Road do not follow modern Silverthorne Road and Cokesbury Road closely; they were not used for control.
Placed from one hand-picked point (Fairview Avenue / Cregar Road) with rotation from the part's north arrow. Low confidence away from that junction.

Printed sheet 3, 100 ft to an inch, north about 16 degrees. Part 1 Mill Street (now Fairview Avenue), Mine Road, Church, Taylor, Thomas and Seal Streets, Mountain Avenue, Silverthorn to the borough line; part 2 an outlined wedge at the upper left with Fairview Avenue, Silverthorn, German Valley Road and the reservoir at the borough limits (north about 4 degrees).

sheet-4-1.description: The Taylor-Wharton Iron and Steel Co. steel works, the largest part of Sheet 4, drawn at 50 feet to an inch (twice the scale of the other sheets) with the compass at the top of the page, although the street and buildings it shares with sheet 1 put north about 17 degrees anticlockwise of the page. The works fill the ground between the South Branch of the Raritan River at the top left and Washington Avenue (Mill) along the right edge, which turns at the bottom right to meet East Main Street and Dewey Avenue. The buildings are numbered: the fetling shop (No. 1) and dry sand foundry (No. 2) with the annealing department and its furnaces, the chain shop, core room and machine shop, shipping department, drafting offices, pattern houses, carpenter shops, storage buildings, a hospital, washrooms, the Bessemer and turbine house, sand and mixing houses, and a water cooling pond near the bottom. Railroad sidings fan in from the top right and along the right side, with a trestle beside Washington Avenue. A note gives the works' watchman, power, heating, lighting and fire protection, including a Worthington fire pump. The fire department (L.H. Taylor Hose Co.) stands at the corner of Washington Avenue and East Main Street. Heavy lines separate the foundry, the electric power plant and the machine shop, which are drawn at other angles.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch; the other sheets are at 100 feet.
The road lettered Washington Av. (Mill) along the east side of the works has no modern counterpart; only its south end at East Main Street survives as Washington Avenue.
The foundry, electric power plant and machine shop parts of this sheet were not placed.

Placed from one hand-picked point (East Main Street / Washington Avenue) at the scale bar (7.9 px/ft) with a rotation of -16.7 degrees, fitted to the water cooling pond, shed No. 10 and the junction as also drawn on sheet 1; the compass on this sheet points about 15 degrees off that. Low confidence away from the lower right corner.

Printed sheet 4, 50 ft to an inch (scale bar), compass about -2 degrees, but part 1 fits at -16.7 degrees against features shared with sheet 1. Taylor-Wharton Iron and Steel Co. Four parts divided by heavy lines: part 1 the Steel Works between the South Branch and Washington Avenue (Mill), with East Main Street and Dewey Avenue at the lower right corner; part 2 the Foundry on Mill Street (upper left, north about 60 degrees); part 3 the Electric Power Plant (lower left); part 4 the Machine Shop (lower middle). Parts 2 to 4 have no street junction that survives and were not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Taylor-Wharton Iron and Steel Co. Foundry on Mill Street (Washington Avenue), with the pond and Y.M.C.A. (no street junction on the part; its Mill Street could not be matched to a modern street line with confidence; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet 2 part 1 or sheet 4 part 1 if a shared feature is identified, or parcel corners of the works site).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Taylor-Wharton Iron and Steel Co. Electric Power Plant (flume from Lake Solitude) (no street junction or modern feature on the part; needs step 6b: hand-picked control (Columbia Trail, former Dover Branch, or parcel corners), not available from the modern street data).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Taylor-Wharton Iron and Steel Co. Machine Shop (main office, water cooling pond) (no street junction on the part; needs step 6b: hand-picked control from parcel corners or a neighbouring sheet).
